plain: Researcher Matthew LaCroix tells Jesse Michels that, drawing on the ancient writer Plutarch and a figure named Sonchis, the Temple of Sais in ancient Egypt existed to keep records of history. LaCroix says the temple was destroyed sometime within 500 to 1,000 years after the Greek visitor Solon heard its stories, so those records were lost, which would mean a key archive of very ancient history vanished.
